--- title: "[StepNormalize]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Center and scale numeric columns to zero mean and unit variance. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_normalize.py#L122-L240){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepNormalize(columns, id=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each selected numeric column ``x`` is replaced in place by ``(x - mean) / std``, using the column's mean and standard deviation. Constant (zero-variance) columns among the selection cannot be scaled to unit variance; they are dropped from the normalization (with a warning) and pass through ``transform`` untouched. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Selector]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns to normalize. Accepts a single column name, a list of names, a shoez selector such as ``Selectors.numeric_predictors()`` (see `Selectors` for the full set), or a narwhals or polars selector (``narwhals.selectors.numeric()``, ``polars.selectors.numeric()``). Selectors are resolved against the frame's schema when the recipe is fitted, so the same selector works on any backend. Only numeric columns are meaningful here. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"normalize"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each selected column is replaced in place by its centered, unit-variance values: ::: {#d2f0e814 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]}) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
x
0 1.0
1 2.0
2 3.0
3 4.0
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#df04163b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_predictors())) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_normalize(select(role='predictor', type=NumericType)) [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` learns each column's mean and standard deviation: ::: {#e6b6fe2e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 1 columns — 1 predictor Steps: step_normalize(x) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` applies them in place: ::: {#1e026235 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
x
0 -1.161895
1 -0.387298
2 0.387298
3 1.161895
``` ::: :::
